text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the new code works together with the existing code. As part of the process, the system runs tests automatically to find problems. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become bigger and harder to fix. CI pipelines often include several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. By using CI, teams can save time, improve code quality, and release software more quickly and safely.
